items.title: Bersatu Padang Besar hit by mass exodus as 20 leaders quit party
items.summary: PADANG BESAR, Sept 9 — A total of 20 Bersatu leaders in the Padang Besar Division, including its deputy chief and vice-chief, have announced their immediate resignation and departure from the party. Besides the division’s deputy chief, Ramzi Md Udi, others include its vice-chief Ramli Aripin, Acting Srikandi (Women’s) chief Fazuwin Razak, Srikandi Muda (Women’s Youth) Chief Nurul Hafiza Ramli and 14 of its 24 branch leaders. “After examining the situation and holding in-depth discussions with fellow leaders, including the 14 branch chiefs from the Padang Besar Division, we have reached a consensus to resign and leave Bersatu.

items.title: FDS team in Sarawak helicopter crash was serving remote communities
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 9 —The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) team involved in the helicopter crash near Long Lellang this afternoon is one of the active teams providing healthcare services to residents in remote areas of Sarawak. According to the Ministry of Health (MOH), the FDS was introduced in Sarawak in 1973 and plays a vital role in delivering healthcare services to communities in hard-to-reach areas. Dr Veronica said the FDS deployed a comprehensive medical team comprising a doctor, nurses and an assistant medical officer to ensure patients received holistic care.

items.title: Father says doctor killed in helicopter crash returned to Sarawak just two days ago
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 9 — The father of one of the victims of the helicopter crash in Sarawak, Kamarudin Salleh, said he last met his daughter, Dr Ainul Baroah, when she came home for the school holidays before returning to Sarawak on Sunday. Kamarudin, 69, said his daughter was quiet, kind towards her family and always willing to help. Kamarudin said he received news of the incident at 5 pm yesterday from one of his daughter’s parents-in-law.

items.title: 'Empower communities, build trust to ensure disaster preparedness' - Dr Mexmollen Marcus
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: When an earthquake with a magnitude of 6.0 struck Mount Kinabalu on June 5, 2015, Dr Mexmollen Marcus learned that there were serious gaps in the authorities' response to such a disaster. Recalling his experience as an on-call junior doctor who was stranded at Panalaban for three days following the earthquake, he said emergency response was severely hampered by bad weather and the lack of previous joint disaster exercises. The Universiti Malaysia Sabah Faculty of Medicine deputy dean added that poor communication and information-sharing, lack of trust, unclear roles and fragmented governance were among the recurring weaknesses in disaster response.

items.title: Pilot, four Health Ministry personnel confirmed dead in Long Lellang helicopter crash
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 9 — A pilot and four Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel were confirmed dead after the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter they were travelling in crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) yesterday afternoon. Miri Division resident and chairman of the Miri Division Disaster Management Committee, Galong Luang, confirmed that all five people on board the helicopter died in the crash, which occurred at about 3.40 pm. Earlier, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the helicopter departed from Miri, and besides the pilot, those onboard were a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses, all of whom were on official duty.

items.title: Azeez Rahim to face corruption charge today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim will first be brought before the Sessions Court for a separate remand proceeding before facing a corruption charge today. His lawyer, Datuk Abu Bakar Isa Ramat, said Azeez, 60, was arrested by the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department yesterday afternoon before being taken to the Dang Wangi police station. "The police will apply for a remand order under Section 420 of the Penal Code," he said when met at the court complex lobby.

items.title: 25 years after 9/11, Americans fear domestic extremists more than foreign attacks: Poll
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Twenty-five years after the Sept 11 attacks focused US fears on threats from abroad, Americans are now considerably more worried about attacks by domestic extremists than by foreign groups, a Reuters/Ipsos poll found. When asked to name the biggest threat to the safety of average Americans, 33 per cent of respondents picked "domestic terrorism," while 20 per cent picked foreign terror and 42 per cent pointed to random acts of violence such as mass shootings, the Aug 28-31 poll found. Reuters/Ipsos polling from mid-2013 showed 21 per cent of Americans viewed domestic terror as the top threat, less than the 28 per cent who pointed to foreign terror and 51 per cent who picked random acts of violence.

items.title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Air accident investigators to arrive in Miri today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) team is expected to arrive in Miri today to begin investigating the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak. Norazman said a Fire and Rescue Department helicopter carrying 18 personnel from various agencies departed Miri for Long Lellang at 7am. "Four police personnel from Long Lama and four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency personnel from Miri are also en route to Long Lellang," he said.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar amid rate-hike expectations
items.summary: Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said higher US Treasury yields suggested that the Federal Reserve could opt for a higher benchmark interest rate when the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on Sept 15-16. "The US Treasury notes auction for three-month and six-month bills yielded higher at 3.80 per cent and 3.89 per cent, respectively," he told Bernama. Mohd Afzanizam also said the Japanese yen strengthened against the US dollar to 153.53 yen, reflecting growing expectations that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) could raise its policy rate, supported by signs of stronger economic performance.

items.title: Oil prices climb as Mideast war flares
items.summary: AFP HONG KONG: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday to near US$100 a barrel in early Asia trade, as war in the Middle East threatened to further choke supply from the crude-rich region. The price of Brent crude, the benchmark international contract, rose to US$99.38 per barrel, while the main US contract West Texas Intermediate was at US$94.51 per barrel. Iran said on Wednesday it struck a US military base in Jordan and that it would target oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for US strikes on its vessels.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB denies Zahid involved in bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has denied claims that Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was involved in attempts to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang diPertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan. Ismail said he hoped the issue concerning Negeri Sembilan’s customs and traditions would be resolved amicably and in accordance with the law, in the interests of stability, harmony and the well-being of the people. “Following a report published by The Straits Times today (Sept 8), I wish to deny claims that UMNO president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was involved in any attempt to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang diPertuan of Negeri Sembilan,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Wall Street down, oil up as inflation, Middle East worries persist
items.summary: All three major US indices dipped Tuesday, kicking off a holiday-shortened week on a lower note. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 1.18 per cent, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.58 per cent and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.32 per cent. Brent crude oil was up 2.13 per cent to US$99.07 a barrel and US crude jumped 2.82 per cent to US$94.05 a barrel.

items.title: A community brought together through faith and prayers [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For residents of Taman Bukit Maluri, the annual Hungry Ghost Festival is more than a religious observance. At the annual Hungry Ghost Festival celebration organised by Persatuan Yee Lan Guan Yin Ting Bukit Maluri Kepong at the Guan Yin Ting temple, preparations began more than two months ago. The association's secretary, Cheah Hong Kee, said the festival welcomes anyone who wishes to pray with a sincere heart.

items.title: Superyacht Marina to secure Lima's future?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Malaysia Bhd's planned superyacht marina can help position Langkawi as a higher-value maritime and tourism hub, while boosting its appeal to high-spending visitors. UniKL Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said the proposed marina could complement Lima's existing defence, aerospace, maritime and tourism pillars by adding luxury yachting and marine conventions. He described Lima as the "best marketing tool" for the marina, saying the combination could help position Langkawi as a regional maritime hub.

items.title: PuTERA35 aims to boost Bumiputera contribution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is exploring interventions under the Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035 (PuTERA35) to double the contribution of Bumiputera micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035. The proposal was among the key areas discussed at the Bumiputera Wealth Creation and Corporate Empowerment Forum held here on Monday, which focused on strengthening business growth, asset ownership and economic participation. "This requires us to build more Bumiputera companies capable of expanding at a larger scale, competing in high-value sectors and subsequently increasing Bumiputera economic participation," he said.

items.title: Trump seeks swift Ukraine war end, restored US-Russia ties
items.summary: MOSCOW: Donald Trump told Russian President Vladimir Putin by phone on Tuesday that he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine, which would allow US-Russia ties to be fully restored, the Kremlin said, adding that Putin had supported the US president's view. The call, which the Kremlin said lasted an hour, followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who are trying to revive stalled talks designed to find a way to end the fighting. Trump, Ushakov said, had made it clear he wanted the war quickly finished.

items.title: As Umno general assembly begins today, Malay unity, PAS-PN ties and the battle for Melaka set to dominate discussions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno’s general assembly begins today with the party facing a question that has become increasingly difficult to avoid: what does it want to be when the next general election arrives? It is also the party’s second general assembly this year. But the assembly comes at a consequential juncture for Umno.

items.title: Run further in Pos Malaysia Run 2026!
items.summary: POS Malaysia Run 2026 is returning to Dataran Merdeka here on Nov 29. This year, the organisers are introducing the 21km Open and Veteran categories for the third edition of the community event. Building on last year's turnout of more than 7,000 runners, Pos Malaysia is targeting 10,000 participants for this year's edition.

items.title: Smart mission in Nepal starts
items.summary: THE Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) MAS-01 has reached Trishuli Bazar, Nepal and is preparing to begin humanitarian efforts and search for 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable. "The 11 members have arrived and are based at a military camp, though the name of the camp was not specified," said National Disaster Management Agency director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim yesterday. Meanwhile, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Malaysia's rescuers had the technological expertise needed to support complex SAR operations, although he was unsure of the specific equipment deployed with the team.

items.title: UK, France, Canada to ban imports from Israeli settlements
items.summary: LONDON: Britain, France and Canada said Tuesday they will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with a UK minister accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians there. The trio of Western allies revealed the trade curbs in response to Israel's West Bank settlements policy and reports of increasing attacks by settlers there against Palestinians. "The British government agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank – perpetrated by settler terrorists," said Britain's foreign minister Ed Miliband, announcing the import ban and other measures in parliament.

items.title: MAG expands Asean travel pacts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group Bhd (MAG) is expanding its partnerships with travel industry associations in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines, as it seeks to widen distribution and customer reach across key regional markets. MAG expects the partnerships to support incremental revenue and travel demand while strengthening Kuala Lumpur's role as a regional aviation hub. In Thailand, MAG will work with the Thai Travel Agents Association through the Thai International Travel Fair to support consumer engagement and travel demand.

items.title: Social media firms that flout 'duty of care' face hefty Aussie fines
items.summary: SOCIAL MEDIA giants face A$109 million fines if they fail to protect young users from harmful content, said Australia's prime minister yesterday as he unveiled draft laws reining in big tech. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese released draft laws that would place a "duty of care" on the firms behind popular platforms such as Facebook, TikTok and Instagram. Social media companies would be held responsible for protecting under-18s from pornography, online bullying, content that glorified crime and content that encouraged eating disorders.

items.title: Doctor killed in helicopter crash returned to Sarawak just two days ago - Father
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Dr Ainul Baraah, who was killed in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, had returned to the state just two days ago after spending a week on holiday with her family in Kelantan. "My daughter had only returned to Sarawak two days ago after spending a week here. Today, we received news that the helicopter she was travelling in had crashed and that she had died," Kamaruddin Salleh, 69, said when contacted.

items.title: Azeez Rahim detained ahead of graft charges, says son
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has been detained by Dang Wangi police ahead of an expected remand, his son said. Azeez's son, Azman Azeez, said in a Facebook post that his father was supposed to appear at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow to face graft charges. "I do not want to pre-empt the court process.

items.title: Bersatu Padang Besar rocked as members from 14 branches quit party
items.summary: PADANG BESAR: Members from 14 of the 24 Bersatu branches in Padang Besar have quit the party with immediate effect, effectively crippling the division. Padang Besar Bersatu deputy chief Ramzi Md Udi said the decision was made after they lost confidence in the party's central leadership. Also leaving the party were division deputy chief Ramli Aripin, acting division Srikandi chief Fazuwin Razak and division Srikandi Muda chief Nurul Hafiza Ramli.

items.title: Heli crash: Kelantan MB offers condolences over doctor's death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud has expressed condolences over the death of Kelantan-born doctor Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, who was killed in a helicopter crash near Long Lellang, Sarawak. He said Dr Ainul died while serving those in need, providing medical care and hope to communities. A BO-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Sarawak.

items.title: 11 men to be charged over Penang armed riot
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Eleven men will be charged tomorrow over an armed riot involving two Gang 04 groups in Air Itam here. The incident occurred on Aug 29, with the clash involving the two groups outside SJK(C) Kong Min Second Branch. On Sept 4, media reports said police had arrested 10 more local men in connection with the armed riot involving the two Gang 04 groups.

items.title: Elderly motorcyclist dies after collapsing on road
items.summary: TAMPIN: An elderly man died after he collapsed while riding a motorcycle along Jalan Tampin-Gemas near Pekan Tampin here this afternoon. Tampin district police chief Superintendent Amiruddien Sariman said the 65-year-old local man was believed to have been riding against traffic flow when the incident occurred at about 2.30pm. "Initial investigations found that the victim was travelling from Kampung Baru towards Pekan Tampin.

items.title: Dr Ainul's mother struggles to accept daughter's death after Sarawak heli crash
items.summary: KOTA BARU: "Even now, I still cannot accept the news that Ainul has left us forever." Those were the words of Rogayah Mohd Nor, 69, mother of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, who died in a helicopter crash in Sarawak this afternoon. She said there had been no unusual changes in her daughter during the week she returned to her hometown for a holiday last week.

items.title: NST Leader: Scammers are evolving, the law must keep up
items.summary: For most Malaysians, this common-sense response is the first line of defence against scam calls. Last year, 73 per cent of surveyed Malaysians admitted to being deceived by various scams, but most common were recorded phone scams, with 28,388 cases. Across various digital and phone channels, 66,204 cases were recorded as cyber fraud surged nationwide.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz's position: MB denies Ahmad Zahid's involvement
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has denied claims that Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was involved in attempts to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang diPertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan. "Following a report published by The Straits Times today (Sept 8), I wish to deny claims that Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was involved in any attempt to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang diPertuan of Negri Sembilan," he said in a statement today. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Fire and Rescue team to assist in Long Lellang helicopter crash probe
items.summary: KUCHING: The Fire and Rescue Department's northern region airbase team will be deployed to Long Lellang tomorrow morning to assist in the investigation into this afternoon's helicopter crash. "I am deeply saddened to receive news of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter accident at the Long Lellang STOLport this afternoon. A BO-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport.

items.title: US sanctions threaten to crush Iranian students' dreams
items.summary: Nikki had been due to take the TOEFL English proficiency test, a key qualification required by many foreign universities, in Iran later this month. Now, like many Iranian students dreaming of a future elsewhere, she is scrambling to find another way to take it, while absorbing the new exam fee and hefty travel costs. On its website, ETS said Iranians could still travel abroad to take the exams.

items.title: How 2 men survived 9 days in hydropower tunnel after Nepal floods
items.summary: A DELIRIOUS Kabir Maharjan drifted in and out of consciousness in a pool of muddy water in complete darkness, trapped for nine days in a tunnel beneath the wreckage of Nepal's worst flood disaster in decades. He and mechanical foreman Sanjay Sah survived in an air-filled chamber, said lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane, a veteran tunnel engineer who helped lead the rescue effort. "I have to go inside the tunnel," he told her.

items.title: Five media workers lose contact while covering Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: JAKARTA: Five Indonesian media personnel reportedly lost contact while covering the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau near Sebesi Island, Lampung, southern Sumatra, not far from the volcano, today. Banten Search and Rescue (SAR) Office Chief Al Amrad said the joint SAR team was still conducting an intensive search operation to locate all the media personnel. "Search and rescue teams are still searching for the five media personnel who lost contact.

items.title: Pilot's wife asks for prayers after Sarawak heli crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq has asked for prayers for her husband after the Long Lellang helicopter crash today. Another user, Fazeera_ilyas said: "Stay strong sis. Stnrlrznh said: "My condolences, sis.

items.title: Malaysia’s SMART team arrives in Nepal disaster zone, begins drone reconnaissance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) arrived in Dhunche, Nepal, today to establish a forward base and begin aerial reconnaissance operations using drones in the disaster-stricken area. According to a statement issued by the Home-Based Support Team (HBST) of MAS01 SMART, under the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), the 10-member team, led by Inspector Abdullah Ahmad Sobri, travelled to the location aboard an MI-17 helicopter. “Dhunche serves as the tactical forward base for managing disaster operations in the Rasuwa area, covering Timure, Syafrubesi, Dhunche and Mailung.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Status of five aboard Flying Doctor Service helicopter still unknown after Sarawak crash
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the helicopter, which departed from Miri, was carrying a pilot and four MOH health personnel — a medical officer, medical assistant and two nurses — who were on official duty. “Based on the initial information received, the flight that departed from Miri was operated by one pilot and carried four MOH health personnel, namely one medical officer, one medical assistant and two nurses who were on official duty,” he said in a statement. CAAM said the BO-105 helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service flight with five people on board, including the pilot.

items.title: Turkish Airlines will be new Liverpool shirt sponsor in £300m deal
items.summary: LONDON, Sept 8 — Turkish Airlines will become Liverpool’s new front-of-shirt sponsor from the start of the 2027/28 season, the Premier League giants announced today. In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than £700 million for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League. Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez to be charged tomorrow over RCI-linked probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009. On Aug 27, the former TH chairman and former Treasury secretary-general were each remanded for seven days, until Sept 2, to assist investigations following disclosures related to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. The RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, also identified investments requiring a forensic audit.

items.title: Flying Doctor Service helicopter carrying five crashes near Long Lellang airport
items.summary: KUCHING, 8 Sept — A BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) airport, about 929 kilometres north of Kuching, today. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58 pm. The helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service flight with five people on board, including the pilot, CAAM said in a statement.

items.title: MACC: Political Financing Bill should set clear penalties, ensure independent enforcement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Political Financing Bill should set clear penalties for political parties that breach contribution limits or fail to report their funding, while also establishing an independent regulatory body to ensure the law is effectively enforced. Deputy director of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) National Governance Planning Division Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the matter is among five key governance principles to consider when drafting the Bill. He said the five principles comprised transparency, accountability, equity and fairness, independence, and inclusiveness and participation.

items.title: Zaid urges Putrajaya to safeguard Petronas interests in Sarawak talks
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to ensure the federal government and Petronas’ interests are protected as Putrajaya continues negotiations with Sarawak over the state’s oil and gas rights. In a post on X, Zaid expressed concern that political considerations could influence the government’s handling of Sarawak’s demands, particularly over Petros’ role as the state’s sole gas aggregator. “Anwar must not exchange political support for oil and gas to Sarawak,” he said.

items.title: Johor orders hunt for five feral dogs after girl mauled in Batu Pahat
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — The Johor government has directed a large-scale operation to hunt and capture five feral dogs that attacked a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak in Batu Pahat last weekend. Johor religious committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said efforts are being carried out by the Batu Pahat district office in collaboration with the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police. Mohd Fared said the immediate capture of the feral animals involved needs to be carried out to ensure that they are free of rabies.

items.title: Johari: Parliamentary Service Act gives Parliament greater scope to strengthen oversight of government
items.summary: CAMERON HIGHLANDS, Sept 8 — The implementation of the Parliamentary Service Act (PSA) provides Parliament with the scope to streamline its legislative role, including strengthening special select committees to assist the government in identifying shortcomings and addressing public issues, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul. He said the enactment of the PSA created a new environment after Parliament operated under executive oversight for 33 years, enabling the legislative body to play a more independent role in contributing to national prosperity. He said under the 10 ministry-related committees established, each is comprised of 12 Members of Parliament (MPs) representing both government and opposition backbenchers who do not hold ministerial or deputy ministerial posts.

items.title: Brothers get High Court leave to challenge DBKL approval for 39-storey towers near their Old Klang Road home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Two brothers have obtained High Court permission to challenge Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s approval for two 39-storey residential towers planned less than 11 metres from their home along Jalan Klang Lama. The judge also granted an interim stay on the development until the brothers’ application for a permanent stay is heard on October 8, despite an objection from the Attorney General’s Chambers. The proposed project is expected to have 1,544 residential units, with the brothers also seeking general damages and costs.

items.title: AI-powered traffic centre launched to boost safety, speed up response on three Klang Valley highways
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — With rising traffic volumes and frequent incidents putting greater pressure on highway operators, a new smart traffic control centre covering three major Klang Valley highways was launched today to enhance road safety and enable faster responses through real-time monitoring. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said past data showed that 85.4 per cent of traffic accidents on tolled expressways last year were attributed to human factors, while the remainder involved vehicle and environmental factors. Meanwhile, IJM’s AI-powered smart expressway traffic control centre integrates 144 CCTV cameras, 87 Video Incident Detection System units, 35 Automatic Number Plate Recognition units and 22 VMS units for the three aforementioned expressways.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Anak Krakatau ash could reach Malaysia, but risk remains low
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The risk of volcanic ash from Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau reaching Malaysia is currently low, although changes in wind direction and speed as well as possible further eruptions could affect its movement, MetMalaysia said today. “Information from global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centres (VAACs) also allows any potential movement of the ash into Malaysian airspace to be identified and communicated to the public promptly,” he said. Earlier, media reports said continued eruptions from Anak Krakatau since Friday had spread volcanic ash and prompted six airports to suspend flight operations.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Malaysia could see temperatures hit 40°C from January to May 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia could experience extreme heat and dry weather from January to May next year, with temperatures in some areas potentially reaching 40°C as a very strong El Nino, or Super El Nino, is expected to develop towards the end of this year. He said past meteorological records showed that very strong El Nino episodes were often associated with higher temperatures, dry weather and a serious risk of haze, similar to conditions currently affecting the country. Mohd Hisham said there was about a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the current El Nino would exceed the strength of any El Nino episode recorded since 1950.

items.title: Senior medical officer in Melaka remanded over RM1.5m knee implant supply probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A senior medical officer has been remanded for five days to assist a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into alleged abuse of position involving the supply of knee implants worth about RM1.5 million. The remand order for the man, in his 50s, was issued by Ayer Keroh Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman at the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court in Melaka this morning, Harian Metro reported. The public servant has been remanded until September 12 after MACC applied for the order to facilitate further investigations.

items.title: Anwar to chair MA63 meeting on Sabah’s 40pc revenue claim, says Hajiji
items.summary: Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said Sabah would host the meeting, which would also discuss outstanding claims and issues under MA63, Sinar Harian reported. He said this after a working visit to the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant in Kunak today. However, there are still other matters, including the 40 per cent payment,” he said.

items.title: Former minister released on MACC bail over Tabung Haji RCI probe, chief commissioner confirms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — A former minister who was remanded over an investigation linked to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail today. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the release, Sinar Harian reported today. “He (the former minister) has been released on MACC bail,” he said today.

items.title: Should political parties’ donors be protected? Azalina says issue among those being studied
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — If Malaysia were to have a law regulating donations to political parties, should it protect donors from being pursued by anti-corruption investigators after donating money? Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that this was among the technical issues that have to be studied before steps are taken to introduce a political financing law in Malaysia. she said.

items.title: Nazir Razak, Musa Hitam say NEP fostered ‘tongkat culture’ among Malays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The New Economic Policy (NEP) fostered a culture of dependency among Malays and became too focused on ownership and government assistance, former CIMB Group chairman Tan Sri Nazir Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Musa Hitam said today. Nazir said the NEP was intended to run for only 20 years and cited former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman’s description of it as a 20-year “handicap”. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” said Nazir, the son of second prime minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.

items.title: Did the Negeri Sembilan MB sign decree to oust ruler? Claim sees state in renewed palace crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Negeri Sembilan has been thrust again into its unprecedented constitutional crisis, with claims that new Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim allegedly signed a proclamation to depose the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, just one day after swearing an oath of allegiance to him. According to the statement released by the four chieftains, Ismail met them on August 3 alongside throne contender Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, the cousin of Tuanku Muhriz and son of the previous ruler. The chieftains alleged that Ismail signed the formal proclamation ousting Tuanku Muhriz during this gathering, paving the way for Tuanku Nadzaruddin’s installation.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt agencies to work together to tighten e-commerce rules, curb sale of prohibited goods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Communications Ministry is prepared to work with the Home Ministry, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, police and relevant agencies to strengthen e-commerce regulation and curb the sale of prohibited goods, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said most e-commerce platforms in Malaysia prohibit the sale of prohibited products, including drugs such as fentanyl, but expressed concern that one platform appeared to be too lax in allowing such products to be offered. “The accounts selling these prohibited products may be fake accounts,” he said.

items.title: Azalina: Malaysians want political funding law before GE16; political parties’ buy-in needed to avoid delay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysians have voiced their desire for Malaysia to have a political financing law to regulate political parties’ funding before the 16th general election, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today. Azalina said the views of political parties would have to be obtained before the proposed political financing law is brought to Parliament, as it would be politicians in Parliament who would vote on whether to introduce such a law. Earlier in the speech, Azalina said BHEUU had taken over studies on the proposed political financing law since May 2023, and that the Cabinet had on September 8, 2023 agreed in principle to the enactment of the law and decided on further studies on the policy scope.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng hits PAS over failure to credit him for cutting lottery draws from 22 to eight a year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at PAS over what he described as dishonest and hypocritical claims about DAP’s position on Islam, while pointing to his record of reducing special lottery draws when he was finance minister. In a Facebook post, Lim said PAS had failed to acknowledge that he was the first finance minister to reduce the number of special lottery draws from 22 to eight a year when Pakatan Harapan (PH) was in government from 2018 to 2020. “PAS is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year during the PH government from 2018 to 2020,” he said.

items.title: IBS classrooms to ease overcrowding in Melaka schools, says deputy education minister
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 8 — The construction of additional classrooms using the Industrialised Building System (IBS) will enable special rooms currently used as temporary teaching and learning spaces to resume their original functions, said Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh. He said the move would help ease overcrowding while enabling schools to make better use of their existing facilities. “Some schools have had to convert special rooms, including music rooms and laboratories, into classrooms.

items.title: Blocked trails delayed six hikers’ return from Gunung Gerah, says Perak Fire Dept
items.summary: GERIK, 8 Sept — The closure and obstruction of hiking trails that have not been used for a long time were the main reasons why the six hikers took a longer time to make their way before they were found safe last night, after participating in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, on August 29. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the hikers found that the trails at Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat were closed due to these factors. “When they reached Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat, the found that the trails to both these hills were closed as they had not been used by hikers for a long time.
